concerns.text: Task T013 explicitly states 'do NOT attempt to read CRS... Infer... or assume WGS84', which semantically weakens FR-001 and US-1 Acceptance Scenario 3. The spec mandates 'automatically reprojects all coordinates' for mismatched systems (e.g., NAD83). Assuming WGS84 without detection is a silent relaxation of the requirement to handle coordinate mismatches.

Tasks T031a and T032a conflate sensitivity analysis with FDR control. FR-006 requires FDR application to p-values 'when testing multiple hypotheses simultaneously across different song metrics'. The tasks aggregate p-values from Model A/B outputs into a single list, rather than applying FDR to the set of p-values generated across the {0.01, 0.05, 0.10} threshold sweep required by SC-003 and FR-004. This drops the acceptance criterion for stability measurement.

Task T031 defines Jaccard index calculation as comparing sets at 'each threshold pair', which implies pairwise comparison. SC-003 requires measuring 'stability' by calculating the Jaccard index 'across the {0.01, 0.05, 0.10} range' as a single aggregate evidence point. The task description risks producing pairwise metrics instead of the required stability aggregate, dropping the acceptance criterion.

Constitution Principle V (Versioning Discipline) requires dynamic updates to `state/projects/...yaml` `updated_at` and `artifact_hashes` on every artifact change. T004 only initializes the file. T011/T012/T017 mention 'updating' in descriptions but lack a dedicated task to implement the state-file-updating mechanism logic. This creates a risk of the state file becoming stale, violating the constitution's versioning discipline.

Task T016 specifies writing to `data/logs/excluded_species.json` but does not include a step to create the `data/logs/` directory. T004 only creates `data/raw/` and `data/processed/`. Without explicit directory creation, the script will crash, violating Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) which requires 'runnable end-to-end without manual intervention'.
